request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each user can now choose which people-list columns their screen shows, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**What changed**
- **New `src/main/frontend/features/people/ColumnChooser.tsx`:** a set of checkboxes with `data-testid="column-<name>"`, one per column. All columns are on when the screen first opens. The columns you switch off are kept in the URL as a `hideColumns` setting, the same way the existing sort-by and show-retired toggles work. So the choice belongs to that user's screen, stays when the sheet is reloaded, and doesn't affect what another user sees.
- **`PeopleList.tsx`:** the chooser sits next to Sort by. A column you switch off loses both its header and its cells, so it has no cell on the screen at all. Totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are unchanged.

**Decisions for you**
- **I added an `excess` checkbox that the request doesn't list.** The test hides `excess` along with the 14 listed columns and expects its cell to disappear, so it needed a checkbox too.
- **The choice isn't saved on the server.** It lives with the screen. A user who signs in from a fresh browser starts with every column shown. The request doesn't say the choice must survive a new sign-in and the test doesn't check it. Saving it per user on the server would mean a new table and endpoint, which I can add if you want it to follow the user.

No server, stored-data or audit changes were needed, since changing columns writes nothing.
